export default function GoalMessages() {
  const { isSignedIn, getToken } = useAuth();
  const online = useOnlineStatus();
  const [threads, setThreads] = useState<DmThreadSummary[] | null>(null);
  const [listError, setListError] = useState("");
  const [listAttempt, setListAttempt] = useState(0);
  const [thread, setThread] = useState<DmThread | null>(null);
  const [openError, setOpenError] = useState<{ id: number; message: string } | null>(null);
  const [threadError, setThreadError] = useState("");
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState("");
  const [sending, setSending] = useState(false);
  const [followRule, setFollowRule] = useState<DmFollowRequired | null>(null);
  const [sendBlock, setSendBlock] = useState<DmSendBlock | null>(null);
  const [unsent, setUnsent] = useState("");
  const composerRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
  const inFlightRef = useRef(false);
  /** The conversation on screen, so a late answer for another one is not shown here. */
  const openCounterpartRef = useRef<number | null>(null);

  const authedFetch = async (path: string, init?: RequestInit) => {
    const token = await getToken();
    try {
      return await fetch(path, { ...init, credentials: "include", headers: { ...(init?.headers ?? {}), ...(token ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {}) } });
    } catch { throw new Error(NETWORK_ERROR); }
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!isSignedIn) return;
    let active = true;
    setThreads(null); setListError("");
    void authedFetch("/api/dms/threads").then(async response => {
      const payload = await readApiJson<{ threads?: DmThreadSummary[]; error?: string }>(response, LIST_ERROR);
      if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || LIST_ERROR);
      if (active) setThreads(payload.threads ?? []);
    }).catch(reason => { if (active) setListError(reason instanceof Error ? reason.message : LIST_ERROR); });
    return () => { active = false; };
  }, [isSignedIn, listAttempt]);

  const resetChat = () => { setThreadError(""); setFollowRule(null); setSendBlock(null); setDraft(""); setUnsent(""); };

  const openThread = async (counterpartUserId: number) => {
    // A draft belongs to one conversation: never carry it into another.
    resetChat(); setOpenError(null);
    openCounterpartRef.current = counterpartUserId;
    try {
      const response = await authedFetch(`/api/dms/threads/${counterpartUserId}`);
      const payload = await readApiJson<{ thread?: DmThread; sendBlock?: unknown; error?: string }>(response, OPEN_ERROR);
      if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || OPEN_ERROR);
      if (openCounterpartRef.current !== counterpartUserId) return;
      setThread(payload.thread ?? null);
      setSendBlock(parseDmSendBlock(payload.sendBlock));
      const pending = readPendingSend(DM_SEND_WORKFLOW, { recipientKey: String(counterpartUserId) });
      if (pending) setDraft(current => (current === "" ? pending.body : current));
    } catch (reason) {
      if (openCounterpartRef.current === counterpartUserId) setOpenError({ id: counterpartUserId, message: reason instanceof Error ? reason.message : OPEN_ERROR });
    }
  };

  const closeThread = () => { openCounterpartRef.current = null; setThread(null); setOpenError(null); resetChat(); };

  const send = async () => {
    if (!thread || sending || inFlightRef.current || !online) return;
    const recipientUserId = thread.counterpartUserId;
    const normalized = normalizeMessageBody(draft);
    if (!normalized) return;
    inFlightRef.current = true;
    setSending(true); setThreadError(""); setFollowRule(null);
    try {
      const { record: attempt } = beginPendingSend({ workflow: DM_SEND_WORKFLOW, recipientKey: String(recipientUserId), body: normalized });
      const response = await authedFetch(`/api/dms/threads/${recipientUserId}`, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", "Idempotency-Key": attempt.idempotencyKey },
        body: JSON.stringify({ body: normalized }),
      });
      const payload = await readApiJson<{ message?: { id?: number }; error?: string; retryAt?: string | number }>(response, SEND_ERROR);
      if (response.status === 201 || response.status === 200) {
        const acknowledgedId = typeof payload.message?.id === "number" ? payload.message.id : null;
        setThread(current => {
          if (!current || current.counterpartUserId !== recipientUserId) return current;
          if (acknowledgedId !== null && current.messages.some(message => message.id === acknowledgedId)) return current;
          return { ...current, messages: [...current.messages, { id: acknowledgedId ?? Date.now(), body: attempt.body, createdAt: new Date().toISOString(), isMine: true }] };
        });
        clearPendingSend(DM_SEND_WORKFLOW);
        if (openCounterpartRef.current === recipientUserId) { setDraft(""); composerRef.current?.focus(); }
        return;
      }
      const block = response.status === 403 ? parseDmSendBlock(payload) : null;
      if (block) {
        clearPendingSend(DM_SEND_WORKFLOW);
        if (openCounterpartRef.current === recipientUserId) { setUnsent(attempt.body); setDraft(""); setSendBlock(block); }
        return;
      }
      const memberRule = response.status === 403 ? parseDmFollowRequired(payload) : null;
      if (memberRule) { if (openCounterpartRef.current === recipientUserId) setFollowRule(memberRule); return; }
      if (response.status === 409) {
        clearPendingSend(DM_SEND_WORKFLOW);
        if (openCounterpartRef.current === recipientUserId) setThreadError("That send changed while retrying, so we kept your text and did not send a duplicate. Review it and send again to start a fresh attempt.");

import React, { createContext, useCallback, useContext, useEffect, useMemo, useRef } from "react";
import { AuthKitProvider as WorkOSAuthKitProvider, useAuth as useWorkOSAuth } from "@workos-inc/authkit-react";
import { setGlobalAccessToken } from "./accessToken";
import { trpc } from "@/lib/trpc";
import { identifyClarity } from "@/lib/clarity";
import { smokeState } from "@/contexts/smokeRuntime";
import { safeAuthReturnTo } from "@shared/authReturnTo";

/**
 * WorkOS AuthKit provider exposing the app's auth hook surface.
 *
 * ~20 call sites import useAuth/useUser/SignInButton from @/_core/auth.
 * Production auth is WorkOS AuthKit, so this module re-exposes the app's
 * shared hook surface on top of the WorkOS context.
 *
 * - useAuth()  -> { isLoaded, isSignedIn, userId, getToken, signOut, openSignIn }
 * - useUser()  -> { isLoaded, isSignedIn, user } (compat user shape)
 * - openSignIn routes to AuthKit; SignInButton navigates to AuthKit.
 * - getToken() resolves null: server routes authenticate via the
 *   app_session_id cookie (AuthKit fetch sends credentials: include).
 */

type EmailAddress = { emailAddress: string; verification: { status: string } };
type CompatUser = { id: string; fullName: string | null; imageUrl: string | null; primaryEmailAddress: { emailAddress: string } | null; emailAddresses: EmailAddress[] } | null;

type CompatValue = {
  isLoaded: boolean;
  isSignedIn: boolean;
  userId: string | null;
  getToken: () => Promise<string | null>;
  signOut: (options?: { returnTo?: string }) => Promise<void>;
  user: CompatUser;
  openSignIn: (options?: { returnTo?: string }) => void;
};

type CompatSdkAuth = {
  isLoading: boolean;
  user: { id: string; email: string; emailVerified: boolean; firstName?: string | null; lastName?: string | null; profilePictureUrl?: string | null } | null;
  signIn: () => Promise<void>;
  getAccessToken: () => Promise<string | null>;
  signOut: (options?: { navigate: false }) => Promise<void>;
};

const CompatContext = createContext<CompatValue | null>(null);

function CompatShell({ children, sdkAuth }: { children: React.ReactNode; sdkAuth: CompatSdkAuth }) {
  const auth = sdkAuth;
  // Server cookie session is the source of truth: it works for BOTH auth planes
  // (WorkOS AuthKit sign-in AND the referrer work-email OTP login). The AuthKit
  // SDK only knows its own PKCE session, so OTP users would look signed out.
  const synthetic = smokeState().active ? smokeState().identity : undefined;
  const meQuery = trpc.auth.me.useQuery(undefined, { retry: false, refetchOnWindowFocus: false, enabled: !synthetic });
  const utils = trpc.useUtils();

  const serverUser = meQuery.data ?? null;
  const signedIn = Boolean(synthetic) || Boolean(serverUser) || Boolean(auth.user);
  const isLoaded = Boolean(synthetic || serverUser) || (!meQuery.isLoading && !auth.isLoading);
  const signingOut = useRef(false);

  const user: CompatUser = synthetic
    ? { id:String(synthetic.id), fullName:`Synthetic ${synthetic.role}`, imageUrl:null, primaryEmailAddress:{emailAddress:synthetic.email}, emailAddresses:[{emailAddress:synthetic.email,verification:{status:"verified"}}] }
    : auth.user
    ? {
        id: auth.user.id,
        fullName: [auth.user.firstName, auth.user.lastName].filter(Boolean).join(" ") || null,
        imageUrl: auth.user.profilePictureUrl ?? null,
        primaryEmailAddress: { emailAddress: auth.user.email },
        emailAddresses: [{ emailAddress: auth.user.email, verification: { status: auth.user.emailVerified ? "verified" : "unverified" } }],
      }
    : serverUser
      ? {
          id: String(serverUser.id),
          fullName: serverUser.name || null,
          imageUrl: null,
          primaryEmailAddress: serverUser.email ? { emailAddress: serverUser.email } : null,
          emailAddresses: serverUser.email ? [{ emailAddress: serverUser.email, verification: { status: "verified" as const } }] : [],
        }
      : null;

  const openSignIn = useCallback((options?: { returnTo?: string }) => {
    // An explicit click must not disappear while either client auth plane is
    // loading. The server still owns authentication; this only starts its flow.
    // Known signed-in users keep their existing session without another flow.
    if (signedIn) return;
    const returnTo = safeAuthReturnTo(options?.returnTo ?? window.location.href, window.location.origin) ?? "/";
    window.location.href = `/api/auth/workos/sign-in?${new URLSearchParams({ returnTo })}`;
  }, [signedIn]);

  // Publish the SDK access token for non-React API clients (tRPC link).
  useEffect(() => {
    let cancelled = false;
    const publish = async () => {
      if (!auth.user) { setGlobalAccessToken(null); return; }
      try {
        const token = await auth.getAccessToken();
        if (!cancelled && !signingOut.current) {
          setGlobalAccessToken(token);
          if (token) await utils.auth.me.invalidate();
        }
      } catch { if (!cancelled) setGlobalAccessToken(null); }
    };
    void publish();
    return () => { cancelled = true; };
  }, [auth.user, auth.getAccessToken, utils]);

  // Clarity replay identity: internal person id only, never raw email.
  // No-op until Clarity init succeeds; nothing to reset on sign-out.
  useEffect(() => {
    identifyClarity(user?.id ?? null);
  }, [user?.id]);

  const signOut = useCallback(async (options?: { returnTo?: string }) => {
    signingOut.current = true;
    try {
      let response = await fetch("/api/auth/workos/logout", { method: "POST", credentials: "include" });
      if (response.status === 404) response = await fetch("/api/dev-auth/logout", { method: "POST", credentials: "include" });
      if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Sign out could not be completed. Please try again.");
    } catch (error) {
      signingOut.current = false;
      throw error;
    }
    try { await auth.signOut({ navigate: false }); } catch {}
    setGlobalAccessToken(null);
    try { sessionStorage.removeItem("manus-cookie"); } catch {}
    await utils.auth.me.cancel();
    utils.auth.me.setData(undefined, null);
    // Callers may bring the person back to a same-origin page (e.g. an OAuth consent screen with its query).
    window.location.href = safeAuthReturnTo(options?.returnTo, window.location.origin) ?? "/";
  }, [auth.signOut, utils]);

  const getToken = useCallback(async () => {
    try { return await auth.getAccessToken(); } catch { return null; }
  }, [auth.getAccessToken]);

  const value = useMemo<CompatValue>(
    () => ({ isLoaded, isSignedIn: signedIn, userId: user?.id ?? null, getToken, signOut, user, openSignIn }),
    [isLoaded, signedIn, getToken, signOut, user, openSignIn],
  );

  return <CompatContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</CompatContext.Provider>;
}

function ServerSessionCompatProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  // No AuthKit client id (local dev / SDK-free mode): run the same compat
  // surface with a neutral SDK layer so consumers still get the server
  // cookie session via tRPC auth.me.
  const neutral = useMemo(() => ({
    isLoading: false,
    user: null,
    signIn: async () => { window.location.href = "/api/auth/workos/sign-in"; },
    getAccessToken: async () => null,
    signOut: async () => { /* handled by the compat signOut */ },
  }), []);
  return <CompatShell sdkAuth={neutral}>{children}</CompatShell>;
}

export function AuthProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const clientId = import.meta.env.VITE_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID || "";
  if (!clientId) {
    // Misconfiguration should be loud in the console, not a blank page.
    console.error("[auth] VITE_WORKOS_CLIENT_ID is not set; falling back to server-session-only auth");
    return <ServerSessionCompatProvider>{children}</ServerSessionCompatProvider>;
  }
  return (
    <AuthKitErrorDowngrade>
      {(downgrade) => downgrade
        ? <ServerSessionCompatProvider>{children}</ServerSessionCompatProvider>
        : <WorkOSAuthKitProvider clientId={clientId} onRefresh={({ accessToken }) => setGlobalAccessToken(accessToken)}>
            <AuthKitInner>{children}</AuthKitInner>
          </WorkOSAuthKitProvider>}
    </AuthKitErrorDowngrade>
  );
}

class AuthKitErrorDowngrade extends React.Component<{ children: (downgrade: boolean) => React.ReactNode }, { error: Error | null }> {
  state = { error: null as Error | null };
  static getDerivedStateFromError(error: Error) { return { error }; }
  render() {
    // false = use the live AuthKit SDK; true = AuthKit render failed, fall back
    // to the server-cookie-only compat layer instead of blanking the route.
    return this.props.children(Boolean(this.state.error));
  }
}

function AuthKitInner({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const auth = useWorkOSAuth();
  return <CompatShell sdkAuth={auth}>{children}</CompatShell>;
}

function useCompat(hookName: string): CompatValue {
  const value = useContext(CompatContext);
  if (!value) throw new Error(`${hookName} must be used within <AuthProvider> (WorkOS-backed)`);
  return value;
}

export function useAuth() {
  const compat = useCompat("useAuth");
  return { isLoaded: compat.isLoaded, isSignedIn: compat.isSignedIn, userId: compat.userId, getToken: compat.getToken, signOut: compat.signOut, openSignIn: compat.openSignIn };
}

export function useUser() {
  const compat = useCompat("useUser");
  return { isLoaded: compat.isLoaded, isSignedIn: compat.isSignedIn, user: compat.user };
}

export function SignInButton({ children, className }: { children?: React.ReactNode; className?: string }) {
  const compat = useCompat("SignInButton");
  // Many sign-in gates pass their own styled <button> as the child. Rendering
  // it inside our <button> would nest interactive elements (invalid HTML,
  // React DOM errors, unreliable clicks), so adopt a button child instead:
  // keep its styling/content and add the sign-in action to its own node.
  if (React.isValidElement(children) && children.type === "button") {
    const child = children as React.ReactElement<{ onClick?: (event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void; className?: string }>;
    return React.cloneElement(child, {
      className: [child.props.className, className].filter(Boolean).join(" ") || undefined,
      onClick: (event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => {
        child.props.onClick?.(event);
        if (!event.defaultPrevented) compat.openSignIn();
      },
    });
  }
  return <button type="button" className={className} onClick={() => compat.openSignIn()}>{children ?? "Sign in"}</button>;
}

export function SignedIn({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return useCompat("SignedIn").isSignedIn ? <>{children}</> : null;
}

export function SignedOut({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return useCompat("SignedOut").isSignedIn ? null : <>{children}</>;
}

import Messages from "../../Messages";

const now = new Date().toISOString();
const memberBlock = { reason: "referrer_acceptance_required", error: "Messages with a referrer open after they accept your request.", senderRole: "member" };
const referrerBlock = { reason: "referrer_acceptance_required", error: "You can message this member after you accept their referral request.", senderRole: "referrer" };
const followRule = { reason: "mutual_follow_required", error: "You can message this member once you follow each other." };
const summary = (id: number, label: string, mine: boolean, unread = 0) => ({ counterpartUserId: id, counterpartLabel: label, lastMessageBody: mine ? "Thanks again" : "Happy to help", lastMessageIsMine: mine, lastMessageAt: now, unreadCount: unread });
const thread = (id: number, label: string) => ({ counterpartUserId: id, counterpartLabel: label, messages: [{ id: 1, body: "Happy to help", createdAt: now, isMine: false }] });

type Reply = { status: number; body: unknown } | "network" | (() => Promise<{ status: number; body: unknown }>);
const server = {
  threads: [] as unknown[],
  listReply: null as Reply | null,
  threadReply: {} as Record<number, Reply>,
  sendBlock: {} as Record<number, unknown>,
  postReply: null as Reply | null,
  posts: [] as { url: string; key: string | undefined; body: unknown }[],
  gets: [] as string[],
};
function respond(reply: { status: number; body: unknown }) {
  return { ok: reply.status >= 200 && reply.status < 300, status: reply.status, json: async () => reply.body } as Response;
}
async function resolveReply(reply: Reply) {
  if (reply === "network") throw new TypeError("Failed to fetch");
  return respond(typeof reply === "function" ? await reply() : reply);
}
beforeEach(() => {
  flagState.on = true; authState.isSignedIn = true;
  server.threads = [summary(22, "Referrer · acme.com", true), summary(33, "Member · Asha", false, 2)];
  server.listReply = null; server.threadReply = {}; server.sendBlock = {}; server.postReply = null; server.posts = []; server.gets = [];
  Object.defineProperty(window.navigator, "onLine", { configurable: true, value: true });
  vi.stubGlobal("fetch", vi.fn(async (url: string, init?: RequestInit) => {
    if (init?.method === "POST") {
      const headers = (init.headers ?? {}) as Record<string, string>;
      server.posts.push({ url, key: headers["Idempotency-Key"], body: JSON.parse(String(init.body)) });
      if (server.postReply) return resolveReply(server.postReply);
      return respond({ status: 201, body: { message: { id: 99 } } });
    }
    server.gets.push(url);
    if (url === "/api/dms/threads") return resolveReply(server.listReply ?? { status: 200, body: { threads: server.threads } });
    const id = Number(/\/api\/dms\/threads\/(\d+)$/.exec(url)?.[1]);
    if (server.threadReply[id]) return resolveReply(server.threadReply[id]);
    const label = (server.threads as { counterpartUserId: number; counterpartLabel: string }[]).find(item => item.counterpartUserId === id)?.counterpartLabel ?? "Member";
    return respond({ status: 200, body: { thread: thread(id, label), sendBlock: server.sendBlock[id] ?? null } });
  }));
});
afterEach(() => { cleanup(); vi.unstubAllGlobals(); window.sessionStorage.clear(); });
// Warm the lazily loaded goal chunk so a cold transform on a busy runner

const primaries = () => document.querySelectorAll("[data-g-primary]");
/** Opens a chat from its row in the list (the next-step button names the same person). */
async function openChat(name: RegExp) {
  fireEvent.click(within(await screen.findByRole("list", { name: "Chats" })).getByRole("button", { name }));
  return screen.findByRole("heading", { level: 1 });
}

// Assert the page contract only on inbox states with its single next-step block.
// Loading/error and open-chat/pre-acceptance panels intentionally have no such block.
describe("goal /messages: inbox", () => {
  it("flag off keeps the kit page", async () => {
    flagState.on = false;
    server.threads = [];
    render(<Messages />);
    expect(await screen.findByText("Your chats live here.")).toBeTruthy();
    expect(document.querySelector('[data-goal-page="messages"]')).toBeNull();
  });

  it("opens on the goal with the chat waiting on you first and one black commit to answer it", async () => {
    const { container } = render(<Messages />);
    expect(await screen.findByRole("heading", { level: 1, name: "Your chats." })).toBeTruthy();
    const rows = await screen.findAllByTestId("goal-chat-row");
    assertGoalPage(container, GOAL_PAGE);
    expect(rows[0]?.textContent).toMatch(/Member · Asha/);
    expect(rows[0]?.textContent).toMatch(/Waiting on you/);
    expect(rows[1]?.textContent).toMatch(/Referrer · acme\.com/);
    expect(primaries()).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(primaries()[0]?.textContent).toMatch(/Reply to Member · Asha/);
    fireEvent.click(primaries()[0] as HTMLElement);
    expect(await screen.findByRole("heading", { level: 1, name: "Member · Asha" })).toBeTruthy();
    expect(server.gets).toContain("/api/dms/threads/33");
  });

  it("states the acceptance rule in plain words on the inbox", async () => {
    render(<Messages />);
    await screen.findAllByTestId("goal-chat-row");
    expect(screen.getByText(/Messages with a referrer open after they accept your request\./)).toBeTruthy();
  });

  it("an empty inbox points at a referral request and names where those conversations live", async () => {
    server.threads = [];
    const { container } = render(<Messages />);
    expect(await screen.findByText("No chats yet.")).toBeTruthy();
    assertGoalPage(container, GOAL_PAGE);
    expect(screen.getByRole("link", { name: "My requests" }).getAttribute("href")).toBe("/requests");
    expect(primaries()).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(screen.getByRole("link", { name: /Ask for a referral/ }).getAttribute("href")).toBe("/ask");

  it("shows loading while the chats are on their way", async () => {
    let release: () => void = () => {};
    server.listReply = () => new Promise(resolve => { release = () => resolve({ status: 200, body: { threads: server.threads } }); });

    expect(await screen.findByText("Loading your chats…")).toBeTruthy();
    expect(screen.queryByText("No chats yet.")).toBeNull();
    release();
    expect((await screen.findAllByTestId("goal-chat-row")).length).toBe(2);

  it("a failed load renders its error and a retry, never an empty inbox", async () => {

    fireEvent.click(within(alert).getByRole("button", { name: "Try again" }));
    expect((await screen.findAllByTestId("goal-chat-row")).length).toBe(2);

    delete server.threadReply[33];

    expect(await screen.findByRole("heading", { level: 1, name: "Member · Asha" })).toBeTruthy();

describe("goal /messages: a chat", () => {
  it("sends through the idempotent path and shows the sent message", async () => {
    render(<Messages />);
    await openChat(/Member · Asha/);
    fireEvent.change(screen.getByLabelText("Message"), { target: { value: "  Thanks for the help  " } });
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Send message" }));
    expect(await screen.findByText("Thanks for the help")).toBeTruthy();
    expect(server.posts).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(server.posts[0]?.url).toBe("/api/dms/threads/33");
    expect(server.posts[0]?.body).toEqual({ body: "Thanks for the help" });
    expect(server.posts[0]?.key).toMatch(/^[\x21-\x7E]{16,64}$/);
    expect((screen.getByLabelText("Message") as HTMLInputElement).value).toBe("");
    expect(window.sessionStorage.length).toBe(0);
    expect(primaries()).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it("no message box before acceptance: the server's sendBlock replaces the composer as soon as the chat opens", async () => {
    server.sendBlock[22] = memberBlock;
    render(<Messages />);
    await openChat(/Referrer · acme\.com/);
    expect(screen.queryByLabelText("Message")).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.queryByRole("button", { name: "Send message" })).toBeNull();
    const rule = screen.getByTestId("goal-dm-rule");
    expect(rule.textContent).toMatch(/Messages open after acceptance/);
    expect(rule.textContent).toMatch(/Messages with a referrer open after they accept your request\. No plan or follow changes this\./);
    expect(within(rule).getByRole("link", { name: "Go to My requests" }).getAttribute("href")).toBe("/requests");
    expect(document.body.textContent).not.toMatch(/upgrade|premium|\bPro\b|\bMax\b/i);
  });

  it("a referrer who has not accepted is pointed at the company inbox", async () => {
    server.sendBlock[22] = referrerBlock;
    render(<Messages />);
    await openChat(/Referrer · acme\.com/);
    const rule = screen.getByTestId("goal-dm-rule");
    expect(rule.textContent).toMatch(/You can message this member after you accept their referral request\./);
    expect(within(rule).getByRole("link", { name: "Open my company inbox" }).getAttribute("href")).toBe("/inbox");
    expect(screen.queryByLabelText("Message")).toBeNull();
  });

  it("a sendBlock the server did not shape as the rule keeps the composer", async () => {
    server.sendBlock[22] = { reason: "something_else" };
    render(<Messages />);
    await openChat(/Referrer · acme\.com/);
    expect(screen.getByLabelText("Message")).toBeTruthy();
    expect(screen.queryByTestId("goal-dm-rule")).toBeNull();
  });

  it("a 403 refusal on send replaces the composer with the rule as the server worded it and keeps the text copyable", async () => {
    server.postReply = { status: 403, body: memberBlock };
    render(<Messages />);
    await openChat(/Referrer · acme\.com/);
    fireEvent.change(screen.getByLabelText("Message"), { target: { value: "Can you refer me?" } });
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Send message" }));
    const rule = await screen.findByTestId("goal-dm-rule");
    expect(rule.textContent).toMatch(/Messages with a referrer open after they accept your request\./);
    expect(screen.queryByLabelText("Message")).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.getByTestId("goal-dm-unsent").textContent).toMatch(/Can you refer me\?/);
    expect(window.sessionStorage.length).toBe(0);
  });

  it("never carries a refused draft into another chat", async () => {
    server.postReply = { status: 403, body: memberBlock };
    render(<Messages />);
    await openChat(/Referrer · acme\.com/);
    fireEvent.change(screen.getByLabelText("Message"), { target: { value: "Can you refer me?" } });
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Send message" }));
    await screen.findByTestId("goal-dm-rule");
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "All chats" }));
    await openChat(/Member · Asha/);
    expect((screen.getByLabelText("Message") as HTMLInputElement).value).toBe("");
    expect(screen.queryByTestId("goal-dm-rule")).toBeNull();
    expect(document.body.textContent).not.toContain("Can you refer me?");
  });

  it("does not show a late refusal in a chat the member already left", async () => {
    let answer: (value: { status: number; body: unknown }) => void = () => {};
    server.postReply = () => new Promise(resolve => { answer = resolve; });
    render(<Messages />);
    await openChat(/Referrer · acme\.com/);
    fireEvent.change(screen.getByLabelText("Message"), { target: { value: "Can you refer me?" } });
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Send message" }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(server.posts).toHaveLength(1));
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "All chats" }));
    await openChat(/Member · Asha/);
    answer({ status: 403, body: memberBlock });
    await waitFor(() => expect(window.sessionStorage.length).toBe(0));
    expect(screen.queryByTestId("goal-dm-rule")).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.getByLabelText("Message")).toBeTruthy();
  });

  it.each([
    { name: "409 conflict", status: 409, body: {} },
    { name: "429 rate limit", status: 429, body: { error: "You're sending messages too quickly." } },
    { name: "500 server error", status: 500, body: { error: "Message service is down" } },
  ])("does not show a late $name in a different chat", async ({ status, body }) => {
    let release: (value: { status: number; body: unknown }) => void = () => {};
    server.postReply = () => new Promise(resolve => { release = resolve; });
    render(<Messages />);
    await openChat(/Referrer · acme\.com/);
    fireEvent.change(screen.getByLabelText("Message"), { target: { value: "A message for the referrer" } });
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Send message" }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(server.posts).toHaveLength(1));
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "All chats" }));
    await openChat(/Member · Asha/);
    const sendButton = screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Send message" });
    expect(sendButton.getAttribute("aria-busy")).toBe("true");
    release({ status, body });
    await waitFor(() => expect(sendButton.getAttribute("aria-busy")).toBeNull());
    expect(screen.queryByRole("alert")).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.getByLabelText("Message")).toBeTruthy();
  });

  it("the follow rule keeps the draft and offers no upgrade", async () => {
    server.postReply = { status: 403, body: followRule };
    render(<Messages />);
    await openChat(/Member · Asha/);
    fireEvent.change(screen.getByLabelText("Message"), { target: { value: "Hi there" } });
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Send message" }));
    const card = await screen.findByTestId("goal-dm-follow-rule");
    expect(card.textContent).toMatch(/Follow each other to message/);
    expect(card.textContent).toMatch(/You can message this member once you follow each other\./);
    expect((screen.getByLabelText("Message") as HTMLInputElement).value).toBe("Hi there");
    expect(document.body.textContent).not.toMatch(/upgrade|premium|\bPro\b|\bMax\b/i);
  });

  it("a 429 says when to try again and a 409 keeps the text without a duplicate", async () => {
    server.postReply = { status: 429, body: { error: "You're sending messages too quickly." } };
    render(<Messages />);
    await openChat(/Member · Asha/);
    fireEvent.change(screen.getByLabelText("Message"), { target: { value: "Hi" } });
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Send message" }));
    expect((await screen.findByRole("alert")).textContent).toMatch(/You're sending messages too quickly\. Try again in a few minutes\./);
    server.postReply = { status: 409, body: {} };
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Send message" }));
    expect((await screen.findByRole("alert")).textContent).toMatch(/did not send a duplicate/);
    expect((screen.getByLabelText("Message") as HTMLInputElement).value).toBe("Hi");
  });

  it("a send that fails shows the server's words and keeps the text", async () => {
    server.postReply = { status: 500, body: { error: "Message service is down" } };
    render(<Messages />);
    await openChat(/Member · Asha/);
    fireEvent.change(screen.getByLabelText("Message"), { target: { value: "Hello" } });
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Send message" }));
    expect((await screen.findByRole("alert")).textContent).toMatch(/Message service is down/);
    expect((screen.getByLabelText("Message") as HTMLInputElement).value).toBe("Hello");
  });

  it("offline: says so and holds the send", async () => {
    Object.defineProperty(window.navigator, "onLine", { configurable: true, value: false });
    render(<Messages />);
    await openChat(/Member · Asha/);
    expect(screen.getByTestId("goal-offline-state").textContent).toMatch(/offline/);
    fireEvent.change(screen.getByLabelText("Message"), { target: { value: "Hello" } });
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Send message" }));
    expect(server.posts).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});

  if ((out.verdict || out.fixed) && (!out.task || !out.as)) fail("--verdict and --fixed need --task <id> and --as \"<session name>\"");
  if (out.landed && (!out.task || !out.as)) fail("--landed needs --task <id> and --as \"<session name>\"");
  if (out.heartbeat && !out.as) fail("--heartbeat needs --as \"<session name>\" (the name your claim printed)");
  if (out.report && !REPORT_STATUSES.includes(out.report)) fail(`--report is one of ${REPORT_STATUSES.join(", ")}`);
  if (out.report && (!out.task || !out.as)) fail("--report needs --task <id> and --as \"<session name>\"");
  return out;
}

/** The GitHub CLI's token, when an agent is signed in with it; never printed. */
function ghToken() {
  try { return execFileSync("gh", ["auth", "token"], { encoding: "utf8", stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "ignore"] }).trim() || null; }
  catch { return null; }
}

async function github(repo, path) {
  // D-109: any token raises GitHub's limit from 60 reads an hour; `gh auth token` covers agents signed in with the GitHub CLI.
  const token = process.env.GH_TOKEN || process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN || tryGit("config", "--get", "github.token") || ghToken();
  const headers = { accept: "application/vnd.github+json", "user-agent": "skipwait-next-task", ...(token ? { authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {}) };
  const res = await fetch(`https://api.github.com/repos/${repo}${path}`, { headers, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15_000) });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`GitHub ${path} answered ${res.status}`);
  return res.json();
}

/**
 * D-237: one read per branch, shared by the marker list and the `work` flag. Marker commits are empty: a
 * commit that changes files is work, whatever its subject says (D-190).
 */
function commitsOn(ref) {
  return parseProvenanceLog(tryGit("log", "--reverse", "--no-merges", `--format=${PROVENANCE_LOG_FORMAT}`, "--name-only", `origin/main..${ref}`) ?? "");
}

const markersOn = commits => commits.flatMap(({ sha, subject, body, files }) => {
  const m = files.length ? null : parseMarker(subject);
  return m ? [{ ...m, sha, body, ...(m.verb === "Verdict" ? { reviewed: /^reviewed ([a-f0-9]{40})$/m.exec(body)?.[1] ?? null } : {}) }] : [];
});

function loadBranches(tasks) {
  const wanted = new Set([...tasks.flatMap(t => [t.branch, reviewLockOf(t), architectLockOf(t), heartbeatOf(slugOf(t.branch))]), LAND_SLOT]);
  const slugs = tasks.map(t => `/${slugOf(t.branch)}`);
  const refs = git("for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname:strip=3)%09%(committerdate:unix)%09%(objectname)", "refs/remotes/origin/agent");
  const branches = new Map();
  for (const line of refs.split("\n").filter(Boolean)) {
    const [name, unix, sha] = line.split("\t");
    const fixMain = name.startsWith("agent/queue/fix-main-") || name.startsWith("agent/heartbeat/fix-main-");
    if (!wanted.has(name) && !slugs.some(s => name.endsWith(s)) && !fixMain) continue;
    const ref = `refs/remotes/origin/${name}`;
    const merged = tryGit("merge-base", "--is-ancestor", ref, "origin/main") !== null;
    const commits = commitsOn(ref);
    // D-237: buildView cannot call git, so the loader reports whether the ref carries a file-changing commit.
    // PICKER-landed-marker-continuity: only provably empty, recognized markers (and no merge commit) beyond main.
    const merges = Number(tryGit("rev-list", "--merges", "--count", `origin/main..${ref}`) ?? NaN);
    branches.set(name, { tipMs: Number(unix) * 1000, tipSha: sha, merged, work: commits.some(c => c.files.length > 0), markerOnly: markerOnlyOf(commits, merges), markers: markersOn(commits) });
  }
  return branches;
}

/**
 * PICKER-landed-marker-continuity: verified merged pull requests for the todo rows whose branch is gone or carries
 * only markers, beyond the newest-100 closed window (S1, S2). Merged pull requests are cached in the clone's git
 * directory (never in the repository); an incomplete or failed read is unknown, which the core never counts as landed.
 */
async function landedEvidenceFor(doc, branches, mergedHeads, closedFirst) {
  if (mergedHeads === null || closedFirst === null) return new Map();
  const candidates = doc.tasks.filter(t => {
    if (t.status !== "todo") return false;
    const info = branches.get(t.branch);
    if (!info) return !mergedHeads.has(t.branch);
    return info.markerOnly === true && !info.merged;
  }).map(t => t.branch);
  if (!candidates.length) return new Map();
  const dir = tryGit("rev-parse", "--git-common-dir");
  const file = dir ? path.join(path.resolve(dir), "skipwait-next-task", "merged-pulls.json") : null;
  let cache = null;
  try { cache = file ? JSON.parse(readFileSync(file, "utf8")) : null; } catch { cache = null; }
  const out = await collectLandedEvidence({
    repo: doc.repo, candidates, firstPage: closedFirst, cache, now: Date.now(),
    fetchPage: page => github(doc.repo, `/pulls?state=closed&sort=updated&direction=desc&per_page=100&page=${page}`),
    verify: pull => verifyMergedPull(pull, { repo: doc.repo, tryGit, mainRef: "origin/main" }),
  });
  try { if (file) { mkdirSync(path.dirname(file), { recursive: true }); writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify(out.cache) + "\n"); } } catch (e) { console.error(`next-task: could not save the merged pull request cache: ${e.message}`); }
  const unknown = [...out.evidence].filter(([, e]) => e.state === "unknown");
  if (unknown.length) console.error(`next-task: landed state UNKNOWN for ${unknown.length} branch(es) (${unknown[0][1].reason}); they are treated as not landed`);
  return out.evidence;
}

/** D-085: every local branch with commits no origin branch has, and every worktree with uncommitted changes. */
function localState() {
  const top = tryGit("rev-parse", "--show-toplevel") ?? ".";
  const worktrees = new Map();
  for (const block of (tryGit("worktree", "list", "--porcelain") ?? "").split("\n\n")) {
    const path = /^worktree (.+)$/m.exec(block)?.[1];
    const branch = /^branch refs\/heads\/(.+)$/m.exec(block)?.[1];
    if (path && branch) worktrees.set(branch, path);
  }
  const local = [];
  for (const branch of (tryGit("for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname:strip=2)", "refs/heads") ?? "").split("\n").filter(Boolean)) {
    const path = worktrees.get(branch) ?? top;
    const unpushed = Number(tryGit("rev-list", "--count", branch, "--not", "--remotes=origin") ?? 0);
    const dirty = worktrees.has(branch) && Boolean(tryGit("-C", path, "status", "--porcelain"));
    if (!unpushed && !dirty) continue;
    const onOrigin = tryGit("rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", `refs/remotes/origin/${branch}`) !== null;
    // ahead: commits only this clone has; null means the branch itself is missing from origin with commits on it.
    local.push({ branch, ahead: onOrigin ? unpushed : (unpushed ? null : 0), dirty, path });
  }
  const mainBehind = tryGit("rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", "refs/heads/main") ? Number(tryGit("rev-list", "--count", "main..origin/main") ?? 0) : 0;
  return { local, mainBehind };
}

/** D-085: the reports the team sent the CEO, newest first (one marker commit each on agent/reports/log), cleaned again on read. */
function loadReports() {
  const raw = tryGit("log", "-n", "500", "--format=%ct%x1f%s%x1f%b%x1e", `refs/remotes/origin/${REPORTS}`);
  if (!raw) return [];
  return raw.split("\x1e").map(rec => rec.trim()).filter(Boolean).flatMap(rec => {
    const [ct, subject, body = ""] = rec.split("\x1f");
    const m = parseMarker(subject ?? "");
    return m?.verb === "Report" ? [{ id: m.id, status: m.status, who: sanitizeName(m.who), at: Number(ct) * 1000, note: sanitizeNote(body) }] : [];
  });
}

const originRef = name => `refs/remotes/origin/${name}`;
const onOrigin = name => tryGit("rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", originRef(name)) !== null;
const tip = name => git("rev-parse", originRef(name));
const base = name => (onOrigin(name) ? tip(name) : git("rev-parse", "origin/main"));

/**
 * Push one empty marker commit onto `parent` as `branch`. Returns the new
 * commit, or null when another agent got there first; any other refusal
 * (auth, a ruleset, the network) stops the run with git's own words.
 */
function pushMarker(branch, parent, subject, body) {
  const sha = git("commit-tree", `${parent}^{tree}`, "-p", parent, "-m", subject, ...(body ? ["-m", body] : []));
  const res = spawnSync("git", ["push", "-q", "origin", `${sha}:refs/heads/${branch}`], { encoding: "utf8", env: GIT_ENV });
  if (res.status === 0) {
    tryGit("update-ref", originRef(branch), sha);
    return sha;
  }
  if (classifyPushError(res.stderr) === "race") return null;
  fail(`could not push ${branch}: ${(res.stderr || res.error?.message || "unknown error").trim()}`);
}

/**
 * D-085: record that `who` is still on a held task. A quiet claim is re-taken on
 * the ref a takeover pushes to (first push wins); a fresh one gets a heartbeat.
 * Returns false when another agent took it first.
 */
function keepClaim(pick, who, branches, provenanceBody) {
  const all = [...(branches.get(pick.work || pick.task?.branch)?.markers ?? []), ...(branches.get(pick.lock)?.markers ?? [])];
  const external = all.some(m => m.id === pick.task?.id && markerReferences(m.body).external);
  const leasePreview = leaseFor(pick, branches, Date.now());
  if (external && (leasePreview.verb !== "Heartbeat" || pick.of === "land")) {
    const refs = markerReferences(provenanceBody);
    const role = ({ review: "review", land: "land", fix: "fix", build: "build" })[pick.of];
    const result = routeIdentity(loadTrustedProvenance(tryGit).registry, refs.route, who, pick.task.id, role);
    if (refs.invalid || !result.ok) fail("external reclaim requires its actual qualified operator route");
  }
  if (pick.of === "land") {
    const slot = landingSlot(branches, Date.now());
    // PICKER-heartbeat-slot-safety: another lander's fresh slot is theirs. Renewing this holder's own LAND lease
    // below never writes it; a free or quiet slot is taken as before (first push wins, a lost race fails closed).
    const othersFresh = Boolean(slot.holder) && slot.holder !== who && !slot.quiet;
    if (!othersFresh && (slot.holder !== who || slot.quiet)) {
      const parent = onOrigin(LAND_SLOT) ? tip(LAND_SLOT) : git("rev-parse", "origin/main");
      const took = pushMarker(LAND_SLOT, parent, markerSubject("Land claim", pick.task.id, who), provenanceBody);
      if (!took) return false;
    }
  }
  const lease = leaseFor(pick, branches, Date.now());
  const subject = markerSubject(lease.verb, lease.id, who);
  let parent = base(lease.ref);
  let sha = pushMarker(lease.ref, parent, subject, lease.verb === "Heartbeat" ? undefined : provenanceBody);
  if (!sha && lease.retry) {
    // Only this holder writes its side heartbeat; a refused one is a stale view, so read it again once.
    // A refused push on a shared lock or a takeover ref means another agent won it: never retry on top of them.
    tryGit("fetch", "-q", "origin", lease.ref);
    parent = base(lease.ref);
    sha = pushMarker(lease.ref, parent, subject, lease.verb === "Heartbeat" ? undefined : provenanceBody);
  }
  if (!sha) return false;
  // A reclaim adds an empty commit to your own branch: move your local copy onto it so your next push is a fast-forward.
  if (lease.reclaim) {
    const localTip = tryGit("rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", `refs/heads/${lease.ref}`);
    const moved = localTip === parent && tryGit("update-ref", `refs/heads/${lease.ref}`, sha, parent) !== null;
    if (localTip && !moved && localTip !== sha) console.error(`next-task: origin/${lease.ref} gained your claim marker; run git merge --ff-only origin/${lease.ref} (or git pull --no-rebase) in your worktree before your next push, and never force-push`);
  }
  return true;
}

async function state() {
  if (tryGit("fetch", "-q", "--prune", "origin") === null) fail("git fetch origin failed; check your network and GitHub access");
  const raw = tryGit("show", `${LIST_REF}:${LIST}`);
  if (raw === null) fail(`${LIST} is missing on ${LIST_REF}`);
  let doc;
  try { doc = JSON.parse(raw); } catch (e) { fail(`${LIST} is not valid JSON: ${e.message}`); }
  // D-202: the decision register is read with the list, from the same ref, and an unreadable
  // register stops the picker: a guess at which decision is newest would hand out stale work.
  const registerRaw = tryGit("show", `${LIST_REF}:${REGISTER}`);
  if (registerRaw === null) fail(`${REGISTER} is missing on ${LIST_REF}; the picker cannot tell which decision is newest`);
  let register;
  try { register = parseDecisionRegister(registerRaw); } catch (e) { fail(`${e.message}; fix the register before any work is picked`); }
  const errors = validateAssignments(doc, p => tryGit("cat-file", "-e", `${LIST_REF}:${p}`) !== null, register);
  if (errors.length) fail(`${LIST} is invalid; tell Claude Code:\n- ${errors.join("\n- ")}`);
  // D-085: every GitHub read is known or unknown; an unknown one stops the picker instead of looking like "nothing there".
  let mainCi = { state: "unknown" }, openPrs = null, mergedHeads = null, closedFirst = null;
  const prCi = new Map();
  try { mainCi = ciStateFromRuns((await github(doc.repo, "/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?branch=main&event=push&per_page=10")).workflow_runs); }
  catch (e) { console.error(`next-task: ${e.message}`); }
  try {
    const pulls = await github(doc.repo, "/pulls?state=open&per_page=100");
    openPrs = new Map(pulls.filter(p => p.head?.repo?.full_name === doc.repo).map(p => [p.head.ref, p.html_url]));
  } catch (e) { console.error(`next-task: ${e.message}`); }
  try {
    const closed = await github(doc.repo, "/pulls?state=closed&sort=updated&direction=desc&per_page=100");
    closedFirst = closed;
    mergedHeads = new Map();
    for (const p of closed) {
      if (!p.merged_at || p.head?.repo?.full_name !== doc.repo) continue;
      if (!mergedHeads.has(p.head.ref)) mergedHeads.set(p.head.ref, new Set());
      mergedHeads.get(p.head.ref).add(p.head.sha);
    }
  } catch (e) { console.error(`next-task: ${e.message}`); }
  // D-109: one read for every pull request's CI (the newest 100 runs, grouped by branch), not one read per branch,
  // so agents without a token stay inside GitHub's 60 reads an hour. A branch with no run among them reads unknown.
  const slugs = doc.tasks.map(t => `/${slugOf(t.branch)}`);
  const heads = [...(openPrs?.keys() ?? [])].filter(head => head.startsWith("agent/") && slugs.some(s => head.endsWith(s)));
  if (heads.length) {
    try {
      const runs = (await github(doc.repo, "/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?per_page=100")).workflow_runs;
      for (const head of heads) prCi.set(head, ciStateFromRuns(runs.filter(r => r.head_branch === head)));
    } catch (e) {
      console.error(`next-task: ${e.message}`);
      for (const head of heads) prCi.set(head, { state: "error" });
    }
    // PICKER-land-exact-head (D-293): find the tip's run when it has aged out of the newest 100 runs.
    for (const head of heads) {
      const ci = prCi.get(head);
      if (ci?.state === "error") continue;
      const tipSha = tryGit("rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", originRef(head));
      if (!tipSha || ci?.sha === tipSha) continue;
      try {
        const runs = (await github(doc.repo, `/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?head_sha=${tipSha}&per_page=10`)).workflow_runs;
        if (Array.isArray(runs) && runs.length) prCi.set(head, ciStateFromRuns(runs));
      } catch (e) {
        console.error(`next-task: ${e.message}`);
      }
    }
    // PICKER-gate-red-review-route (D-291): a red run on the branch's exact tip gets one read of its jobs, so a red
    // that is only the review gate's own step can be handed REVIEW. Fail closed: a missing run id, a run not on the
    // tip, or any fetch or parse error leaves gateOnly false and the picker keeps handing MAKE GREEN.
    for (const head of heads) {
      const ci = prCi.get(head);
      if (ci?.state !== "red") continue;
      ci.gateOnly = false;
      const tipSha = tryGit("rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", originRef(head));
      if (!Number.isSafeInteger(ci.runId) || !tipSha || ci.sha !== tipSha) continue;
      try { ci.gateOnly = gateOnlyRedFromJobs(await github(doc.repo, `/actions/runs/${ci.runId}/jobs?per_page=100`)) === true; }
      catch (e) { console.error(`next-task: ${e.message}`); }
    }
  }
  // Count main-only commits, not branch-only commits. Missing refs stay unknown,
  // never a misleading zero; use argv (not a shell) for branch names from GitHub.
  const prBehind = new Map();
  for (const head of openPrs?.keys() ?? []) {
    const raw = tryGit("rev-list", "--count", `${originRef(head)}..origin/main`);
    const count = raw !== null && /^\d+$/.test(raw) ? Number(raw) : null;
    prBehind.set(head, Number.isSafeInteger(count) ? count : null);
  }
  const branches = loadBranches(doc.tasks);
  const landedEvidence = await landedEvidenceFor(doc, branches, mergedHeads, closedFirst);
  return { doc, register, mainCi, openPrs, mergedHeads, landedEvidence, prCi, prBehind, branches, reports: loadReports() };
}

function claim(pick, who, branches, provenanceBody) {
  const history = [...(branches.get(pick.work || pick.task?.branch)?.markers ?? []), ...(branches.get(pick.lock)?.markers ?? [])];
  if (!provenanceBody && pick.kind !== "continue" && history.some(m => m.id === pick.task?.id && markerReferences(m.body).external)) fail("external task claim requires its actual qualified operator route");
  const origin = () => git("rev-parse", "origin/main");
  switch (pick.kind) {
    case "build": return Boolean(pushMarker(pick.task.branch, origin(), markerSubject("Claim", pick.task.id, who), provenanceBody));
    case "takeover":
    case "green": return Boolean(pushMarker(pick.work, tip(pick.work), markerSubject("Takeover", pick.task.id, who), provenanceBody));
    case "land": {
      const parent = onOrigin(LAND_SLOT) ? tip(LAND_SLOT) : git("rev-parse", "origin/main");
      const tookSlot = pushMarker(LAND_SLOT, parent, markerSubject("Land claim", pick.task.id, who), provenanceBody);
      if (!tookSlot) return false;
      if (pick.tier1) {
        return Boolean(pushMarker(pick.lock, tip(pick.lock), markerSubject("Land claim", pick.task.id, who), provenanceBody));
      }
      return Boolean(pushMarker(pick.work, tip(pick.work), markerSubject("Takeover", pick.task.id, who), provenanceBody));
    }
    case "unblock": return Boolean(pushMarker(pick.lock, pick.lockExists ? tip(pick.lock) : origin(), markerSubject("Unblock", pick.task.id, who), provenanceBody));
    case "architect":
    case "resync": return Boolean(pushMarker(pick.lock, pick.lockExists ? tip(pick.lock) : origin(), markerSubject(pick.lockExists ? "Takeover" : "Claim", pick.task.id, who)));
    case "fix-main": return Boolean(pushMarker(pick.lock, pick.parent ? tip(pick.parent) : origin(), markerSubject(pick.parent ? "Takeover" : "Claim", fixMainIdOf(pick.sha), who)));
    case "review": return Boolean(pushMarker(pick.lock, pick.lockExists ? tip(pick.lock) : origin(), markerSubject("Review claim", pick.task.id, who), provenanceBody));
    case "fix": return branches.has(pick.lock) && Boolean(pushMarker(pick.lock, tip(pick.lock), markerSubject("Fix claim", pick.task.id, who), provenanceBody));
    case "continue": return keepClaim(pick, who, branches, provenanceBody);
    default: return false;
  }
}

function printSync(sync) {
  if (!sync.blocking.length && !sync.notes.length) return;
  console.log("LOCAL WORK ORIGIN CANNOT SEE (D-085):");
  for (const line of sync.blocking) console.log(`- MUST PUSH: ${line}`);
  for (const line of sync.notes) console.log(`- ${line}`);
  console.log("");
}

/** --report and --fixed speak for work that must already be on origin. */
function requireSynced(doc, branches, who) {
  const { local, mainBehind } = localState();
  const sync = localSyncIssues({ local, branches, claimant: who, mainBehind, tasks: doc.tasks });
  if (!sync.blocking.length) return;
  printSync(sync);
  fail("your own work is not on origin yet (the MUST PUSH lines above); push it, then run this again", 3);
}

async function main() {
  const args = argsOf(process.argv.slice(2));
  const date = new Date().toLocaleDateString("en-CA");
  if (args.verdict || args.fixed) {
    const { doc, branches, openPrs } = await state();
    const task = doc.tasks.find(t => t.id === args.task) ?? fail(`no task ${args.task}`);
    const lockName = reviewLockOf(task), lock = branches.get(lockName);
    const stage = reviewStateOf(lock, task.id);
    const holder = stageHolderOf(lock, task.id);
    // PROCESS-review-gate (D-166): the reviewer who passed may re-record the pass on the current head (after a merge of main, or
    // over a verdict written before verdicts named their head); a landing refuses a head no verdict names.
    const reviewer = [...(lock?.markers ?? [])].reverse().find(m => m.id === task.id && m.verb === "Review claim")?.who ?? null;
    const rerecord = args.verdict === "pass" && ["passed", "landing"].includes(stage) && reviewer === args.as;
    if (args.verdict && !rerecord && (stage !== "in-review" || holder !== args.as)) fail(`only the reviewer holding ${lockName} records a verdict (it is ${stage}, held by ${holder ?? "nobody"})`);
    if (args.fixed && (stage !== "fixing" || holder !== args.as)) fail(`only the agent holding the fix claim on ${lockName} marks it fixed (it is ${stage}, held by ${holder ?? "nobody"})`);
    if (args.fixed) requireSynced(doc, branches, args.as);
    const subject = args.verdict ? markerSubject("Verdict", task.id, args.as, args.verdict) : markerSubject("Fixed", task.id, args.as);
    // The body names the head reviewed: the tip of the task's branch on origin now, which the gate compares with the PR head.
    const architect = architectLockOf(task);
    const reviewedBranch = task.status === "architect" && onOrigin(architect) && openPrs?.has(architect) ? architect : task.branch;
    const reviewed = args.verdict ? (onOrigin(reviewedBranch) ? tip(reviewedBranch) : fail(`${reviewedBranch} is not on origin; there is no head to review`)) : null;
    const body = [reviewed ? `reviewed ${reviewed}` : null, args.provenance ? `provenance ${args.provenance}` : null, args.execution ? `execution ${args.execution}` : null].filter(Boolean).join("\n");
    const history = [...(branches.get(reviewedBranch)?.markers ?? []), ...(lock?.markers ?? [])];
    if (args.provenance || history.some(m => markerReferences(m.body).external)) {
      if (!args.provenance || !args.execution) fail("external completion requires qualified route and execution IDs");
      const head = reviewed || tip(task.branch);
      const marker = { id: task.id, who: args.as, verb: args.verdict ? "Verdict" : "Fixed", verdict: args.verdict, reviewed, body };
      const trusted = loadTrustedProvenance(tryGit);
      const result = resolveTaskProvenance({ taskId: task.id, head, workMarkers: branches.get(reviewedBranch)?.markers ?? [], lockMarkers: [...(lock?.markers ?? []), marker], ...trusted, git: tryGit });
      if (!result.ok) fail(`external completion held: ${result.reason}`);
      const model = result.reviewers?.get(args.as);
      if (args.verdict && (!model || [...result.builders, ...result.fixers].includes(model))) fail("external reviewer also built or fixed this work");
    }
    if (!pushMarker(lockName, tip(lockName), subject, body || undefined)) fail(`could not push ${lockName}: it moved; fetch and run again`);
    console.log(`Recorded on ${lockName}: ${subject}${reviewed ? ` (reviewed ${reviewed})` : ""}`);
    return;
  }
  if (args.landed) {
    const { doc, branches } = await state();
    const task = doc.tasks.find(t => t.id === args.task) ?? fail(`no task ${args.task}`);
    const err = releaseLandingSlotError({ branches, task, claimant: args.as, now: Date.now() });
    if (err) fail(err);
    const subject = markerSubject("Landed", task.id, args.as);
    const parent = onOrigin(LAND_SLOT) ? tip(LAND_SLOT) : git("rev-parse", "origin/main");
    if (!pushMarker(LAND_SLOT, parent, subject)) fail(`could not push ${LAND_SLOT}: it moved; fetch and run again`);
    console.log(`Released landing slot ${LAND_SLOT}: ${subject}`);
    return;
  }
  if (args.status) {
    const { doc, register, mainCi, openPrs, mergedHeads, landedEvidence, prCi, prBehind, branches, reports } = await state();
    const newest = register.at(-1);
    console.log(`Register: ${newest.id}, ${newest.date} — ${newest.title}`);
    console.log(`main CI: ${mainCi.state}${mainCi.url ? ` (${mainCi.url})` : ""}${openPrs === null || mergedHeads === null ? " · pull requests: UNKNOWN (GitHub read failed; the board may be wrong)" : ""}\n`);

#!/usr/bin/env node

/**
 * PROCESS-review-gate (D-166, docs/plans/PROCESS-gates.md): a Tier 1 row merges only after an
 * independent pass verdict on its exact head (D-074, D-151).
 *
 *   node scripts/review-gate.mjs        # check the current branch's head now (a lander's check)
 *
 * In CI it runs as its own step, "Review gate (independent Tier 1 pass)" (the name the picker reads,
 * D-286/D-291), and again from `scripts/scope-check.mjs` right after the queue gate, on pull requests
 * only. On actions/checkout's depth-one checkout it first fetches origin/main with history, as the queue
 * gate does (REVIEW-GATE-fetch-parity, D-292), so the named step evaluates instead of failing open.
 * It finds the row as the queue gate does (the row's own branch, or a marker branch of its slug).
 * A Tier 2 or 3 row, or no row, passes here; the queue gate handles the no-row case. For a Tier 1
 * row it reads the row's review lock (`agent/review/<slug>`) and passes only when:
 *   1. the newest stage marker is a pass verdict, or a Land claim whose nearest earlier verdict is a pass;
 *   2. that verdict's body `reviewed <sha>` is the head, or every commit after it in the head's own
 *      history that is not on origin/main is a merge or the status commit a landing makes (a merge of
 *      main and the status commit keep the pass, any other new commit does not);
 *   3. the verdict's author's model neither built (Claim, Takeover on the task branch) nor fixed
 *      (Fix claim, Fixed on the lock) the work (D-151).
 * A bot comment is never a review. Like the queue gate it fails open, loudly, only on its own
 * internal error (no git, an unreadable task list, GitHub unreachable).
 */
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
import { modelOf, parseMarker, reviewLockOf, slugOf } from "./nextTaskCore.mjs";
import { classifyTier, tierReasonPaths } from "./tierClassifyCore.mjs";


const ASSIGNMENTS = "docs/plans/assignments.json";
export const REVIEW_GATE_FAIL = "Tier 1: this head has no independent passing review (D-074, D-151). Run node scripts/next-task.mjs to get a review.";

/** GATE-tier-floor (D-212): a declared Tier 2 row whose changed paths compute Tier 1 (money, sign-in, privacy). */
export const TIER_FLOOR_FAIL = "Tier 1: this change touches";

const SHA = /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/;
const git = args => execFileSync("git", args, { encoding: "utf8", stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"] }).trim();

/** The row a branch belongs to, by the queue gate's rules 1-2; null when none. */
export function findGateRow(tasks, branch) {
  if (!Array.isArray(tasks) || typeof branch !== "string") return null;
  const own = tasks.find(task => task?.branch === branch);
  if (own) return own;
  const marker = /^agent\/(architect|review|heartbeat)\/([^/]+)$/.exec(branch);
  return marker ? tasks.find(task => typeof task?.branch === "string" && slugOf(task.branch) === marker[2]) ?? null : null;

/** The head a verdict names in its marker body (`reviewed <sha>`); null for a verdict written before this gate. */
export function reviewedOf(body) {
  const m = /^reviewed ([0-9a-f]{40})\s*$/m.exec(String(body ?? ""));
  return m ? m[1] : null;
}

const fail = why => `${REVIEW_GATE_FAIL} ${why}`;

export { isStatusOnlyChange } from "./modelProvenance.mjs";

/**
 * The rule, with no I/O. `workMarkers` are the task branch's markers and `lockMarkers` the review
 * lock's, oldest first, each verdict carrying `reviewed` (sha or null). `nonMergeCommitsSince(sha)`
 * lists the head's own non-merge commits after `sha` that are not on origin/main, or returns null
 * when `sha` is not in the head's history. `isStatusCommit(sha)` is true for the status commit a
 * landing makes (`isStatusOnlyChange`), which keeps the pass.
 *
 * GATE-tier-floor (D-212): when `tierOf(changedPaths)` is given, the gate guards the higher of the
 * row's declared tier and the computed tier, so a money or sign-in change filed as Tier 2 still
 * needs the independent pass. Returns null to pass, or the failure message.
 */
export function reviewGateViolation({
  task, head, workMarkers = [], lockMarkers = [], nonMergeCommitsSince, isStatusCommit,
  tierOf, tierReasonPaths = () => [], changedPaths = [], provenance = null,

  if (!task) return null;

  const declared = Number(task.tier);

    ? `${TIER_FLOOR_FAIL} ${tierReasonPaths(changedPaths).map(path => `\`${path}\``).join(", ")}, which are Tier 1 (D-212). It needs an independent pass on its head; correct the row's tier in docs/plans/assignments.json (any session, D-200 (2)).`

  if (last.verb !== "Verdict" && last.verb !== "Land claim") return `${raised} The review of ${task.id} stands at "${last.verb}", not a pass.`;
  const verdict = [...stage].reverse().find(m => m.verb === "Verdict");
  if (!verdict || verdict.verdict !== "pass") return `${raised} The newest verdict on ${task.id} is ${verdict ? verdict.verdict : "missing"}, not a pass.`;

  const reviewed = verdict.reviewed ?? null;
  if (!reviewed) return `${raised} The pass by ${verdict.who} was recorded before verdicts named their head: the reviewer re-records it on the current head (node scripts/next-task.mjs --verdict pass --task ${task.id} --as "<session name>"), and nothing is waived.`;

    workMarkers, lockMarkers, isStatusCommit, ...(provenance ?? {}) });
  if (resolved.active) {
    if (!resolved.ok) return `${raised} External provenance held: ${resolved.reason}.`;
    if (!markerReferences(verdict.body).external) return `${raised} External pass requires its qualified execution marker.`;
    const model = resolved.reviewers.get(verdict.who);
    if (!model || [...resolved.builders, ...resolved.fixers].includes(model)) return `${raised} External review is missing or shares a builder/fixer model.`;
    if (last.verb === "Land claim") {
      const refs = markerReferences(last.body);
      const lander = !refs.invalid && refs.route ? routeIdentity(provenance?.registry, refs.route, last.who, task.id, "land") : null;

  const ofTask = markers => markers.filter(m => m && m.id === task.id);
  const builders = ofTask(workMarkers).filter(m => m.verb === "Claim" || m.verb === "Takeover").map(m => modelOf(m.who));

  if (builders.includes(model) || fixers.includes(model)) return `${raised} The pass is by ${model}, the model that ${builders.includes(model) ? "built" : "fixed"} this work; a review must come from another model (D-151).`;
  return null;
}

/** What one non-merge commit changed, for `isStatusOnlyChange`: each file's text on both sides and the changed line numbers. */
function changesOf(sha) {
  // Untrimmed and unbounded by the 1 MB default: line numbers must match the file exactly.
  const show = (rev, path) => {
    try { return execFileSync("git", ["show", `${rev}:${path}`], { encoding: "utf8", maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024, stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"] }); }
    catch { return ""; }

  const paths = git(["diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--no-renames", "-r", "--name-only", sha]).split("\n").filter(Boolean);
  return paths.map(path => {
    const removed = [];
    const added = [];
    for (const m of git(["diff", "-U0", "--no-renames", `${sha}^`, sha, "--", path]).matchAll(/^@@ -(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? \+(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? @@/gm)) {

      for (let i = 0; i < d; i++) added.push(c + i);

    return { path, before: show(`${sha}^`, path), after: show(sha, path), removed, added };
  });

/** True when `sha` is the status commit a landing makes; false on any doubt (the commit then counts as unreviewed). */
function statusCommit(sha) {
  try { return isStatusOnlyChange(changesOf(sha)); } catch { return false; }

const DB_HUNK_START = /^@@ -(?:\d+)(?:,\d+)? \+(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? @@/;
const DECLARATION = /^\s*(?:export\s+)?(?:default\s+)?(?:async\s+)?(?:function\*?|const|let|var|class)\s+([A-Za-z0-9_$]+)/;

/** The name of the outermost function or declaration a hunk sits in, as `server/db.ts` names it. */
export function enclosingName(line) {
  const m = DECLARATION.exec(String(line ?? ""));
  return m ? m[1] : null;
}

/**
 * What the head changed against its merge base with origin/main: the paths, and for `server/db.ts`
 * each hunk's changed lines plus the function each hunk sits in (GATE-tier-floor, D-212).
 */
export function changedPathsOf(head) {
  let base = "";
  try { base = git(["merge-base", "origin/main", head]); } catch { base = ""; }
  if (!base) return [];
  const paths = git(["diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", `${base}..${head}`]).split("\n").filter(Boolean);
  if (!paths.includes("server/db.ts")) return paths;
  const diff = git(["diff", "--no-renames", "-U0", `${base}..${head}`, "--", "server/db.ts"]).split("\n");
  const hunks = [];
  let hunk = null;
  const close = () => { if (hunk) hunks.push({ added: hunk.added, removed: hunk.removed, context: hunk.context }); hunk = null; };
  for (const line of diff) {
    const start = DB_HUNK_START.exec(line);
    if (start) {
      close();
      hunk = { at: Number(start[1]), added: [], removed: [], context: [] };
      continue;
    }
    if (!hunk || /^[+-]{3}/.test(line)) continue;
    if (line.startsWith("+")) hunk.added.push(line);
    else if (line.startsWith("-")) hunk.removed.push(line);
  }
  close();
  const file = (() => { try { return execFileSync("git", ["show", `${head}:server/db.ts`], { encoding: "utf8", maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024, stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"] }); } catch { return ""; } })();
  const lines = file.split("\n");
  for (const h of hunks) {
    h.context = [];
    for (let i = Math.min(h.at, lines.length) - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
      const name = enclosingName(lines[i]);
      if (name) { h.context.push(name); break; }
    }
  }
  return paths.flatMap(path => (path === "server/db.ts" ? hunks.map(h => ({ path, ...h })) : [path]));

/** Empty marker commits on `range`, oldest first, with each verdict's reviewed head. Commits that change files are work. */
function markersIn(range) {
  const raw = git(["log", "--reverse", "--no-merges", `--format=${PROVENANCE_LOG_FORMAT}`, "--name-only", range]);
  return parseProvenanceLog(raw).flatMap(({ sha, subject, body, files }) => {
    const marker = files.length ? null : parseMarker(subject);
    return marker ? [{ ...marker, sha, body, ...(marker.verb === "Verdict" ? { reviewed: reviewedOf(body) } : {}) }] : [];

function pullRequestHead() {
  const eventPath = process.env.GITHUB_EVENT_PATH;
  if (!eventPath) return null;

/**
 * REVIEW-GATE-fetch-parity (D-292): the twin of scripts/queue-gate.mjs:15 ensureOriginMainHistory.
 * Does nothing when origin/main and HEAD already share a merge base; otherwise fetches main into
 * refs/remotes/origin/main (unshallowing a shallow checkout) and re-checks. Throws on a fetch error.

/** Fetch one branch into origin's namespace; false when origin has no such branch. Throws when origin is unreachable. */

    if (!Array.isArray(tasks)) {

    // server/db.ts (a money line, or a function whose name names money).
    const changedPaths = changedPathsOf(head);

      console.log(`review-gate: ${task.id} declares Tier ${task.tier} but its paths compute Tier 1 (${tierReasonPaths(changedPaths).join(", ")}).`);
    }

    const trusted = loadTrustedProvenance((...args) => { try { return git(args); } catch { return null; } });

      || Boolean(trusted.registry?.routes?.some(r => r.taskId === task.id))
      || (trusted.registryError && trusted.registryError !== "no trusted-main provenance registry");
    const lock = reviewLockOf(task);
    const lockMarkers = fetchBranch(lock) ? markersIn(`origin/main..refs/remotes/origin/${lock}`) : [];

      try { git(["merge-base", "--is-ancestor", sha, head]); } catch { return null; }
      return git(["rev-list", "--no-merges", `${sha}..${head}`, "--not", "origin/main"]).split("\n").filter(Boolean);

      task, head, workMarkers, lockMarkers, nonMergeCommitsSince, isStatusCommit: statusCommit,
      tierOf, tierReasonPaths, changedPaths, provenance: { ...trusted, git: (...args) => { try { return git(args); } catch { return null; } } },
    });

    if (violation) {
      console.error(`review-gate: ${task.id} at ${head.slice(0, 8)}: ${violation}`);
      return 1;
    }
    console.log(`review-gate: ${task.id} at ${head.slice(0, 8)} has an independent passing review.`);
    return 0;
  } catch (error) {
    if (externalContext) { console.error("review-gate: external provenance source unavailable; failing closed"); return 1; }
    console.error(`review-gate: could not run (${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}) — not failing the branch.`);
    return 0;
  }
}

if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) {
  process.exitCode = runReviewGate({ local: true });

# External coding-model provenance (D-311)

This support separates the real operator/session from a public external coding model. It does not authenticate a provider cryptographically. It does not qualify this implementation's unknown underlying author or clear held product work. The checked-in registry starts empty.

## Trust boundary and sequence

Both picker and gate read only `origin/main:docs/model-provenance.json`. A candidate file, CLI model name, comment, digest or successful fixture is not qualification. First deliver this tooling through the existing Tier 2 independent-review, required-test and protected-merge path. It cannot authorize its own first merge.

Before starting external work, separately review a task/operator/model route and merge that qualification through the existing protected process. Use a public provider URL, its selected public model name, sanitized retained observation bytes, and independent qualification-review URL. The reviewer checks the actual selection evidence, canonical model identity (including aliases), operator, task, supported roles and limits. A route only permits claims. It proves no completed coding or review execution.

After the actual run, separately review and merge the exact execution receipt onto main before accepting completion. Check the actual input supplied, output received, observed selected model, exact generated patch and commit range, and whether the operator changed semantics. Keep sensitive content out of this public repository. If sanitized evidence is insufficient to qualify authorship, hold it rather than asserting a model identity. No private transcripts, secrets or internal model metadata belong here.

Qualification changes are their own bounded docs work, not candidate self-approval. A qualified route/receipt is an independently reviewed assertion, not a signed provider receipt. Code checks its structure, digests, binding and contribution independence; human/model review establishes whether the asserted observation is true. Revoke a route with `revoked: true`; do not relabel history to clear a hold.

## Registry version 1

Root fields: `version: 1`, `routes: []`, `executions: []`. IDs are unique within each collection, 1-120 ASCII letters/digits/dot/underscore/hyphen, starting with a letter/digit. Artifact strings are nonempty, no control characters other than tab/newline, at most 16 MiB. SHA fields are lowercase hex (40 for commits, 64 for SHA-256).

Each route has:

- `id`, `taskId`, `operator` (exact actual session, not the model), `modelId` (reviewed canonical public identity), `roles` (subset of `build`, `fix`, `review`, `land`), `revoked` (must be explicitly false to use).
- `providerUrl`, `selectedModel`, `observation`, `observationSha256`, `qualificationReview`. Both URLs must be HTTPS. The observation digest binds retained sanitized bytes, not authorship.

For contributor exclusion, a separately reviewed `modelId` may deliberately group observed same-family models under one conservative key. Such a key may over-exclude reviewers but must never split aliases to gain independence or assert an unobserved served checkpoint/API endpoint. `selectedModel` and the retained observation still identify exactly what the provider visibly selected; execution receipts must preserve that distinction.

Each execution has:

- `id`, `routeId`, `taskId`, `operator`, `role`, `claimSha`, `inputSha`, `outputSha`.
- `input`, `output`, `observation`, each with its corresponding `Sha256` digest, and HTTPS `reviewUrl` for separate execution qualification.
- `semanticEdits: false` only when the operator was pure transport. Operator-authored semantic code/test/fix work is unresolved by this version and holds the route. Do not silently call it transport.
- For build/fix: `output` equals the applied `git diff --binary --no-ext-diff INPUT OUTPUT --` string as read by the CLI (outer whitespace trimmed), with `patchSha256` binding those same bytes. Input must precede output, output must precede the evaluated head, and every branch-owned file-changing commit must be covered. Only the existing landing-status exception is allowed outside those ranges. Main merges must have two parents and a main-anchored second parent, and apply exactly the main delta or have an empty supported Git remerge diff. Semantic merge resolutions are not invisible transport. On older Git, overlapping content merges that cannot be proven clean hold rather than guessing.
- For review: `inputSha === outputSha` names the reviewed exact head, `verdict` is `pass` or `findings`, and `output` retains the actual sanitized verdict. A completed verdict marker must name the same reviewed SHA and verdict. Later code invalidates PASS; only existing supported main merges/status-only commits retain it.

The execution must bind the actual same-operator, same-route role claim in the retained task/lock history. Build/Takeover and Fix claims cannot be replaced by another operator's receipt. Unknown or unqualified build/fix markers hold the task, even if a later receipt spans the whole diff. A qualified abandoned build Claim/Takeover with no completed execution and no explicit execution reference may be non-contributing only when its next qualified build claim is in the evaluated head ancestry, and every commit from the old claim through the next claim is a single-parent empty commit. Each parent delta is checked, so edits followed by reverts, merges, missing claims and unreadable history cannot use this exception. No fix-lock interval is inferred empty, since its ancestry differs from the code branch. This exception neither invents an execution nor permits review of unreceipted actual code. Earlier review/findings-only participation does not make someone a code contributor (D-184).

## Commands and markers

Keep the real operator name, for example `Operator · session`, in `--as`/`--claim`. Do not claim to be the external model. Preview without mutation:

```sh
node scripts/next-task.mjs --as 'Operator · session' --provenance ROUTE_ID
```

Claims, takeovers, fixes and landings use the same `--provenance ROUTE_ID` with ordinary `--claim`. A reclaimed stage must preserve its qualified route. Heartbeats preserve ownership and do not assert a new execution. Completed review and fix markers additionally require their qualified receipt:

```sh
node scripts/next-task.mjs --verdict pass --task TASK --as 'Operator · session' --provenance ROUTE_ID --execution EXECUTION_ID
node scripts/next-task.mjs --fixed --task TASK --as 'Operator · session' --provenance ROUTE_ID --execution EXECUTION_ID
```

The normal subject stays attributed to the actual operator. Body lines `provenance ROUTE_ID` and `execution EXECUTION_ID` are unambiguous references, not free model names. Missing, duplicated, malformed, revoked or wrong-task/operator/role evidence holds external work. Failed completion checks write no marker. Normal fast-forward pushes still settle claim races. Ordinary locks, holder checks, dependencies, main-red safety, tests and protections remain in force.

Picker and gate compare canonical actual model identities against every builder/fixer; another session of the same model is not independent. Legacy-only known-prefix behavior remains unchanged, without claiming those old names are newly verified. An external route cannot reinterpret an unknown legacy contributor. No example here is a qualified live execution.
